svg.title: FrontierHarness performance versus direct modeled token cost
svg.desc: A log-scale scatter plot where farther left is lower direct modeled token cost per resolved task and higher is a higher pass rate. Carry is highlighted at 63.3 percent and 1.3666 dollars per resolved task. Among the published directional references, Pi is at 60.0 percent and 2.433 dollars, Codex is at 66.7 percent and 3.468 dollars, DSH Creator is at 63.3 percent and 3.285 dollars, Claude Code is at 63.3 percent and 18.337 dollars, and Exo is at 53.3 percent and 1.045 dollars. Carry lies on the plotted directional efficiency frontier. Other published references: Claude Code 63.3% / $18.337; Codex 66.7% / $3.468; DSH Creator 63.3% / $3.285; DSH Minimal 56.7% / $4.718; DSH PTC 60.0% / $4.577; DSH Standard 60.0% / $3.459; Exo Harness 53.3% / $1.045; Hermes 50.0% / $2.904; Kimi Code 56.7% / $3.647; Oh My Pi 56.7% / $4.746; OpenCode 50.0% / $3.244; Pi 60.0% / $2.433.
svg.text: FrontierHarness: performance vs. direct modeled token cost
Up is better · left is cheaper · cost axis is logarithmic

svg.text: Direct modeled token cost per resolved task → lower is better
Carry: artifact-gated 19 / 30 result. Published points: non-normalized references; use directionally, not as a leaderboard.
Cost is modeled token cost per resolved task; Carry is a lower bound and excludes runner, storage, checkpoint, and GitHub Actions costs.
